title: Fire by Night
subtitle: Leviticus & Numbers in Poems & Pictures
beforeYouBegin:
Leviticus and Numbers are the books of the camp at Sinai and the long road after it. They hold a fire on the altar that must never go out, a handful of flour seasoned with salt, a goat walking alone into the desert, corners of a field left standing for the poor, and a horn that sounds liberty every fiftieth year. Then the camp sets out: a blessing spoken over the people, a cloud by day and fire by night, manna in the dew, a cluster of grapes carried on a pole, a dry rod covered in almond blossoms, water pouring from a rock, a donkey that stops in the road, and six cities with their gates open for anyone who needs to run.

This book walks through them in forty short poems, in five parts: two for Leviticus and three for Numbers. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the books of Leviticus and Numbers alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

parts.title: Part One · The Fire on the Altar
parts.epigraph: Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out.
parts.zh_epigraph: 坛上的火要一直烧着；它不会出去。

parts.title: Part Two · I Will Walk Among You
parts.epigraph: I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you will be my people.
parts.zh_title: 第二部分·我将行走在你们中间
parts.zh_epigraph: 我将行走在你们中间，我将成为你们的上帝，你们将成为我的子民。

parts.title: Part Three · Bless You and Keep You
parts.epigraph: Yahweh bless you, and keep you.
parts.zh_title: 第三部分·祝福你并保守你
parts.zh_epigraph: 耶和华赐福给你，保护你。

parts.title: Part Four · Has His Hand Grown Short?
Part Five · A Star Out of Jacob
parts.epigraph: A star will come out of Jacob.
parts.zh_epigraph: 一颗星将从雅各身上出来。

paintings.title: called
paintings.poem:
the book begins
with a voice
from inside a tent.

not from the mountain now,
with thunder and smoke,

but from a tent
pitched in the middle
of the camp,

among the cooking fires
and the washing
and the children.

everything that follows,
every rule about fire and flour,

is an answer
to one question:

how do people like us
come near?
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look at the stillness of the warmth of the fire in Timothy’s painting: what striving can you lay down as you ponder, “everything that follows, every rule about fire and flour, is an answer to one question: how do people like us come near?” (Leviticus 1:1)?
paintings.zh_poem:
书开始了
有声音
从帐篷内。

现在还没有从山上下来，
伴随着雷声和烟雾，

但从帐篷里
放在中间
营地的，

在炊火之中
和洗涤
和孩子们。

接下来的一切，
关于火和面粉的每一条规则，

是一个答案
对于一个问题：

人们如何喜欢我们
靠近吗？
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 看看蒂莫西画中火焰温暖的静止：当你思考“接下来的一切，关于火和面粉的每一条规则，都是对一个问题的答案：像我们这样的人如何接近？” （利未记 1:1）？

paintings.title: a pleasant aroma
paintings.poem:
smoke going up
in a straight line
on a still morning.

the whole camp
could see it
from their tent doors.

something given away
completely,
turned to fire and air,

and heaven
called it
pleasant.

you might think
what you give up
simply disappears.

it doesn't.
it rises.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Leviticus 1:9, the story turns on the warmth of the fire—and ends with, “you might think what you give up simply disappears. it doesn't. it rises.” What small, unhurried faithfulness is God inviting you into today?
paintings.zh_poem:
烟雾上升
在一条直线上
在一个寂静的早晨。

整个营地
可以看到它
从他们的帐篷门。

赠送的东西
完全,
变成火和空气，

和天堂
称之为
令人愉快的。

你可能会想
你放弃什么
就这样消失了。

事实并非如此。
它上升了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在《利未记》1:9 中，故事以火的温暖为起点，并以“你可能认为你放弃的东西消失了。其实并没有。它会升起。”神今天邀请你进入什么样的小而从容的信实呢？

paintings.title: salt
paintings.poem:
fine flour.
a little oil.
a pinch of frankincense.

and never
forget the salt.

salt doesn't spoil.
it keeps things.

so every small gift,
even a handful of flour,

was seasoned
with a reminder:

this is not a deal
that goes bad.

this is a promise
that keeps.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The world measures life by speed and noise, yet Leviticus 2:13 points us to the quiet centerpiece of “salt” and whispers, “this is a promise that keeps.” How can you practice that unhurried wisdom today?
paintings.zh_poem:
细面粉。
一点油。
一撮乳香。

从来没有
忘记盐。

盐不会变质。
它保留东西。

所以每一份小礼物，
哪怕是一把面粉，

是经过调味的
并有一个提醒：

这不是一笔交易
那会变得很糟糕。

这是一个承诺
那个保留。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 世界以速度和噪音来衡量生命，但利未记 2:13 向我们指出了安静的核心“盐”，并轻声说道：“这是一个信守的诺言。”今天你如何能修习这种从容的智慧呢？

paintings.title: a fifth part more
paintings.poem:
if you took it,
give it back.

if you lied about
what you found,
return it.

and then,
before you go
to the altar,

add a fifth.

not just enough
to make it even.

a little more,
so your neighbor knows
you meant it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The poem closes with a quiet turn: “a little more, so your neighbor knows you meant it.” Where in your life right now does that line hit closest to home?
paintings.zh_poem:
如果你拿走了它，
把它还给我。

如果你撒谎了
你发现了什么，
返回它。

然后，
在你走之前
到祭坛，

添加第五个。

不仅仅是足够
使其均匀。

再多一点，
所以你的邻居知道
你是认真的。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 这首诗以一个安静的转折结束：“多一点，这样你的邻居就知道你是认真的。”现在，这条线在你生活中的哪个地方最贴近你的家？

paintings.title: it shall not go out
paintings.poem:
every morning
someone got up
before the others

and fed it.

a few pieces of wood.
nothing grand.

no one ever saw
the fire lit.
only the fire kept.

that's most of faith,
really.

not the flash
from heaven.

the wood,
every morning,
laid on the coals.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Sometimes a single sentence opens a window in a closed room: how does “the wood, every morning, laid on the coals” (Leviticus 6:12-13) speak to a question you have been carrying lately?
paintings.zh_poem:
每天早上
有人站起来
在其他人之前

并喂它。

几块木头。
没什么了不起的。

没有人见过
火点燃了。
只有火保留着。

这就是最大的信仰
真的。

不是闪光灯
来自天堂。

木头，
每天早上，
放在煤上。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 有时，一句话可以为封闭的房间打开一扇窗户：“每天早晨，把柴放在炭上”（利未记 6:12-13）如何解答您最近一直在思考的问题？

paintings.title: ashes
paintings.poem:
the priest
in his linen clothes
swept up the ashes.

then changed
into plain ones

and carried them
out of the camp
to a clean place.

even the leftovers
of holy things
were handled with care.

no one
is too important
to carry the ashes.

and nothing
you gave to God
is thrown away.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Hold your hands open for a moment before “ashes” (Leviticus 6:10-11): what are you gripping tightly that loosens when you hear, “and nothing you gave to God is thrown away”?
paintings.zh_poem:
牧师
穿着他的亚麻衣服
扫起了灰烬。

然后改变了
变成普通的

并携带它们
走出营地
到一个干净的地方。

就连剩饭剩菜
神圣事物的
被小心处理。

没有人
太重要了
携带骨灰。

什么也没有
你给了上帝
被扔掉了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在“灰烬”之前张开你的双手（利未记 6:10-11）：当你听到“你所献给上帝的东西，没有一样会被丢弃”时，你紧握的是什么东西就松开了？

paintings.title: hands lifted
paintings.poem:
after all the washing
and the waiting
and the careful fire,

Aaron came down
and lifted up his hands
toward the people.

and then
the glory came.

fire from before the Lord,
and the whole crowd
shouting,
falling on their faces.

it all ends
with a blessing.

that's what
the altar was for.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Scripture remembers this moment in Leviticus 9:22-24 not to impress us, but to steady us: when have you seen the truth that “that's what the altar was for” in your own story?
paintings.zh_poem:
洗完之后
和等待
和小心的火，

阿龙下来了
并举起双手
向人民。

然后
荣耀来了。

火从耶和华面前发出，
和全体人群
喊叫，
落在他们脸上。

一切都结束了
带着祝福。

就是这样
祭坛是为了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 圣经在利未记 9:22-24 中记住这一刻，不是为了给我们留下深刻印象，而是为了让我们稳定：你什么时候在你自己的故事中看到“这就是祭坛的用途”的真理？

paintings.title: holy
paintings.poem:
holy
doesn't mean
far away.

it means
set apart,

the way you set apart
the good cup,
the one you keep
for someone you love.

God said,
be holy, as I am.

not,
stay away.

more like,
come be mine.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As your pilgrim lantern pauses at “holy” (Leviticus 11:45), what one honest sentence would you pray beside the quiet centerpiece of “holy” after reading, “God said, be holy, as I am. more like, come be mine”?
paintings.zh_poem:
神圣的
并不意味着
很远。

这意味着
分开，

你与众不同的方式
好杯子，
你保留的那个
为了你爱的人。

神说，
圣洁吧，像我一样。

不，
远离。

更像是
来成为我的吧。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 当你的朝圣灯笼停在“圣洁”（利未记 11:45）处时，在读到“神说，要圣洁，像我一样。更像是，来成为我的”之后，除了安静的“圣洁”核心词之外，你会祈祷哪一句诚实的句子呢？

paintings.title: the living bird
paintings.poem:
the priest
went outside the camp
to find him.

the one who had lived
out there,
away from everyone.

he looked him over,
and the sickness was gone.

and at the end
of the washing,

a bird
was let go
into the open field.

you can go home now.

you are clean.
you are free.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Between the opening line (“the priest went outside the camp to find him”) and the closing thought (“you are clean. you are free”), what is Leviticus 14:7 gently reframing in your own day?
paintings.zh_poem:
牧师
走出营地
找到他。

曾经住过的人
在那里，
远离所有人。

他打量着他，
病就消失了。

最后
洗涤的过程中，

一只鸟
被释放
进入空旷的田野。

你现在可以回家了。

你很干净。
你自由了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在开场白（“祭司到营外去找他”）和结束语（“你是洁净的，你是自由的”）之间，利未记 14:7 在你那个时代温和地重新诠释了什么？

paintings.title: within the veil
paintings.poem:
once a year
one man in plain linen
went behind the curtain

with coals
and two handfuls of incense.

the smoke
covered the mercy seat
like a cloud.

the closest anyone came
to God

was wrapped
in sweetness
and mercy.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Along the road of Fire by Night, “within the veil” (Leviticus 16:12-13) slows us down at the live coal on the altar to remind us: “the closest anyone came to God was wrapped in sweetness and mercy.” Where are you being invited to trade control for trust today?
paintings.zh_poem:
每年一次
一个穿着普通亚麻布的男人
走到幕后

用煤
和两捧香。

烟雾
遮盖施恩座
像一朵云。

最近的人来过
对上帝

被包裹
在甜蜜中
和怜悯。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 沿着夜之火的道路，“在幔内”（利未记16:12-13）让我们在祭坛上的红炭前放慢脚步，提醒我们：“最接近神的人都被甜蜜和怜悯包裹着。”今天你被邀请在哪里用控制权换取信任？

paintings.title: into the wilderness
paintings.poem:
two hands
on a goat's head.
every wrong
named out loud.

then someone led it
past the last tent
and let it go.

it walked
into the desert
and didn't come back.

that's where
your sin went.

not coming back.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If you were walking this road with a close friend and stopped at “into the wilderness” (Leviticus 16:21-22), what would you talk about after reading, “that's where your sin went. not coming back”?
paintings.zh_poem:
两只手
在山羊的头上。
每一个错误
大声说出名字。

然后有人带它
经过最后一个帐篷
并放手吧。

它走了
进入沙漠
并没有回来。

那就是那里
你的罪孽消失了。

不会回来。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果你和一位亲密的朋友一起走这条路，并在“进入旷野”（利未记 16:21-22）时停下来，当你读到“那是你的罪去的地方，不再回来”之后，你会谈论什么？

paintings.title: the corners of the field
paintings.poem:
don't cut
all the way to the edge.

don't go back
for what you dropped.

don't pick up
the grapes
that fell.

leave them.

someone is coming
later in the day
with an empty basket.

God built
a little room
into your harvest

for people
you've never met.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Pause before the quiet centerpiece of “the corners of the field”: what changes in your posture today when you sit with the closing words of “the corners of the field”—“God built a little room into your harvest for people you've never met”?
paintings.zh_poem:
不要剪
一直到边缘。

不要回去
为了你掉落的东西。

别接
葡萄
那掉下来了。

离开他们。

有人来了
当天晚些时候
带着一个空篮子。

上帝建造的
一个小房间
进入你的收获

为人
你们从未见过。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在《田野的角落》安静的中心部分前停下来：今天，当你坐在《田野的角落》的结束语——“上帝为你从未见过的人的收获中建造了一个小房间”时，你的姿势有什么变化？

paintings.title: as yourself
paintings.poem:
it's here first,
in the middle
of a long list

about wages
and weights
and gossip
and the deaf and the blind.

don't carry a grudge.
don't get even.

love your neighbor
as yourself.

and further down the page,
the stranger too,

because you knew
what it was like
to be one.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look at the stillness of the quiet centerpiece of “as yourself” in Timothy’s painting: what striving can you lay down as you ponder, “and further down the page, the stranger too, because you knew what it was like to be one” (Leviticus 19:18)?
paintings.zh_poem:
它首先在这里，
在中间
一个长长的名单

关于工资
和重量
和八卦
以及聋子和盲人。

不要怀恨在心。
不要报复。

爱你的邻居
就像你自己一样。

并在页面下方，
陌生人也一样，

因为你知道
是什么样的
成为一体。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 看看蒂莫西画作中安静的中心“如你自己”的宁静：当你沉思时，你能放下什么努力，“在页面的下方，陌生人也是如此，因为你知道作为一个人是什么感觉”（利未记19:18）？

paintings.title: the land shall rest
paintings.poem:
six years
you plow.

the seventh,
you don't.

the vine
goes wild.
the field
grows what it likes.

and everyone eats
from it,
the servant and the stranger
and the animals too.

even the dirt
gets a Sabbath.

God is not
in a hurry
to use anything up.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Leviticus 25:4, the story turns on the branches of the vine—and ends with, “God is not in a hurry to use anything up.” What small, unhurried faithfulness is God inviting you into today?
paintings.zh_poem:
六年
你犁地。

第七个，
你不知道。

葡萄树
变得疯狂。
领域
生长它喜欢的东西。

每个人都吃
从中，
仆人和陌生人
还有动物。

甚至污垢
得到一个安息日。

神不是
匆忙
用完任何东西。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在利未记 25 章 4 节中，故事以葡萄树的枝子为中心，并以“神并不急于用完任何东西”作为结尾。神今天邀请你进入什么样的小而从容的信实呢？

paintings.title: jubilee
paintings.poem:
every fiftieth year
a horn
across the whole land.

the field you sold
comes back.

the debt
is gone.

the one who had to work
for his neighbor

walks home
with his children.

the land is mine,
God said.

no one
loses everything
forever.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The world measures life by speed and noise, yet Leviticus 25:10 points us to the quiet centerpiece of “jubilee” and whispers, “no one loses everything forever.” How can you practice that unhurried wisdom today?
paintings.zh_poem:
每五十年
一个喇叭
遍及整个土地。

你卖掉的田地
回来了。

债务
消失了。

必须工作的人
为了他的邻居

步行回家
和他的孩子们。

土地是我的，
神说。

没有人
失去一切
永远。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 世界以速度和噪音来衡量生命，但《利未记》25:10 向我们指出了“禧年”安静的核心，并低语道：“没有人会永远失去一切。”今天你如何能修习这种从容的智慧呢？

paintings.title: I will walk among you
paintings.poem:
after all the fire
and the rules
and the careful distance,

this.

not
I will watch you.

not
I will visit sometimes.

I will walk
among you.

down the rows of tents.
past your door.

the whole book
was leading here.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The poem closes with a quiet turn: “the whole book was leading here.” Where in your life right now does that line hit closest to home?
paintings.zh_poem:
大火过后
和规则
以及谨慎的距离，

这个。

不
我会看着你。

不
我有时会去拜访。

我会走路
你们之中。

沿着一排排的帐篷。
经过你的门。

整本书
正在这里领先。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 这首诗以一个安静的转折结束：“整本书都指向这里。”现在，这条线在你生活中的哪个地方最贴近你的家？

paintings.title: one by one
paintings.poem:
the book of Numbers
begins with names.

not a guess.
not a crowd.

name after name,
family after family,

one by one.

you may feel
like a number.

but in this book
every number
was a name first.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Sometimes a single sentence opens a window in a closed room: how does “but in this book every number was a name first” (Numbers 1:2) speak to a question you have been carrying lately?
paintings.zh_poem:
民数记
从名字开始。

不是猜测。
不是人群。

一个又一个的名字，
一个又一个的家庭，

一一。

你可能会觉得
就像一个数字。

但在这本书里
每个数字
首先是一个名字。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 有时，一句话会在封闭的房间里打开一扇窗：“但这本书中，每一个数字首先都是一个名字”（民数记 1:2）如何解答您最近一直在思考的问题？

paintings.title: around the tent
paintings.poem:
every tribe
had its place,

every family
its banner,

and every tent door
faced the same center.

in the middle
of all that dust
and noise and marching,

a tent
where God lived.

wherever they went,
they set it up first.

and set
their own tents
around it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Hold your hands open for a moment before “around the tent” (Numbers 2:2): what are you gripping tightly that loosens when you hear, “and set their own tents around it”?
paintings.zh_poem:
每个部落
有其一席之地，

每个家庭
它的旗帜，

以及每一个帐篷的门
面对同一个中心。

在中间
所有的灰尘
还有喧闹和行进，

一个帐篷
上帝居住的地方。

无论他们走到哪里，
他们首先设置它。

并设置
他们自己的帐篷
围绕它。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在“围住帐棚”之前（民数记 2:2），请张开双手：当你听到“并在其四围支搭帐棚”时，你紧握的是什么东西就松开了？

paintings.title: bless and keep
paintings.poem:
God gave the priests
their words.

this is how
you bless my people.

say it like this.

he didn't leave it
to chance.

he didn't
let them guess.

he wanted them
to hear
exactly this:

bless you.
keep you.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Scripture remembers this moment in Numbers 6:23-24 not to impress us, but to steady us: when have you seen the truth that “he wanted them to hear exactly this: bless you. keep you” in your own story?
paintings.zh_poem:
神赐予祭司
他们的话。

就是这样
你保佑我的人民。

像这样说。

他没有留下它
机会。

他没有
让他们猜。

他想要它们
听到
正是这样：

祝福你。
留住你。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 圣经在民数记 6:23-24 中记住这一刻，不是为了给我们留下深刻印象，而是为了让我们稳定：你什么时候在你自己的故事中看到过这样的真理：“他希望他们听到这句话：祝福你。保守你”？

paintings.title: his face
paintings.poem:
not his hand
raised against you.

not his back
turned.

his face.

shining.

lifted
toward you.

and at the end
of the blessing,
the thing he wants you
to leave with:

peace.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As your pilgrim lantern pauses at “his face” (Numbers 6:25-26), what one honest sentence would you pray beside your own two hands after reading, “and at the end of the blessing, the thing he wants you to leave with: peace”?
paintings.zh_poem:
不是他的手
反对你。

不是他的背
转身。

他的脸。

灼灼。

举起
向你。

最后
的祝福，
他想要你的东西
离开：

和平。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 当你的朝圣灯笼停在“他的脸”（民数记 6:25-26）时，读完“在祝福的最后，他希望你留下的东西是平安”之后，你会在自己的两只手旁祈祷哪一句诚实的句子呢？

paintings.title: seven lamps
paintings.poem:
the lamps
were turned
to shine forward.

not up
at the gold.

not back
at the one
who lit them.

out,
into the room.

a light
is not for looking at.

it's for seeing by.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Between the opening line (“the lamps were turned to shine forward”) and the closing thought (“a light is not for looking at. it's for seeing by”), what is Numbers 8:2-3 gently reframing in your own day?
paintings.zh_poem:
灯
被转向
闪耀前进。

不起来
在黄金。

不回来
在一个
谁点燃了它们。

出来，
进入房间。

一盏灯
不是用来看的。

是为了看的
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在开场白（“灯转向前照”）和结束语（“光不是用来观看的，而是用来观看的”）之间，民数记 8:2-3 在你那个时代轻轻地重构了什么？

paintings.title: cloud and fire
paintings.poem:
by day
a cloud.

by night
a glow like fire.

a child
could step out of her tent
at midnight

and look
toward the middle of the camp

and see it
still there.

he didn't leave
when it got dark.

he doesn't now.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Along the road of Fire by Night, “cloud and fire” (Numbers 9:15-16) slows us down at the warmth of the fire to remind us: “he didn't leave when it got dark. he doesn't now.” Where are you being invited to trade control for trust today?
paintings.zh_poem:
白天
一朵云。

到了晚上
像火一样的光芒。

一个孩子
可以走出她的帐篷
午夜

看看
朝着营地的中间

并看到它
还在那里。

他没有离开
天黑的时候。

他现在不知道了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 沿着夜火之路，“云与火”（民数记 9:15-16）让我们在火的温暖中放慢脚步，提醒我们：“天黑的时候他没有离开。现在他没有。”今天你被邀请在哪里用控制权换取信任？

paintings.title: a month, or a year
paintings.poem:
sometimes one night.
sometimes a month.
sometimes a whole year
in the same dry place.

when the cloud stayed,
they stayed.
when it moved,
they moved.

some seasons
the faithful thing
is to unpack.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If you were walking this road with a close friend and stopped at “a month, or a year” (Numbers 9:22), what would you talk about after reading, “some seasons the faithful thing is to unpack”?
paintings.zh_poem:
有时一晚。
有时一个月。
有时一整年
在同一个干燥的地方。

当云停留时，
他们留下来了。
当它移动时，
他们搬家了。

一些季节
忠实的东西
就是拆包。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果你和一位亲密的朋友一起走在这条路上，并在“一个月或一年”（民数记 9:22）处停下来，读完“有些季节，忠实的事情就是打开行李”后，你会谈论什么？

paintings.title: a resting place
paintings.poem:
the ark
went out ahead.

three days
ahead of them.

looking
for a place
where they could rest.

you're not
the first one
down this road.

he went ahead
to find
somewhere you can stop.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Pause before the quiet centerpiece of “a resting place”: what changes in your posture today when you sit with the closing words of “a resting place”—“he went ahead to find somewhere you can stop”?
paintings.zh_poem:
方舟
就先出去了。

三天
在他们前面。

寻找
为了一个地方
他们可以休息的地方。

你不是
第一个
沿着这条路。

他继续前进
找到
某个你可以停下来的地方。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在“休息的地方”的安静中心前停顿一下：今天，当你坐下来，以“休息的地方”结束语“他继续寻找你可以停下来的地方”时，你的姿势有什么变化？

paintings.title: the dew
paintings.poem:
every night
while they slept

it came down
with the dew.

small and pale
like coriander seed.

they ground it,
boiled it,
baked it into cakes.

it tasted
like fresh oil.

every morning
enough.

every morning
again.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look at the stillness of the small seed hidden in the soil in Timothy’s painting: what striving can you lay down as you ponder, “every morning enough. every morning again” (Numbers 11:9)?
paintings.zh_poem:
每天晚上
当他们睡觉时

它下来了
与露水。

小而苍白
像芫荽籽。

他们把它接地，
把它煮沸，
把它烤成蛋糕。

它尝起来
像新鲜的油一样。

每天早上
够了。

每天早上
再次。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 看看提摩太画中隐藏在土壤中的小种子的静止：当你沉思“每天早晨够了，又是每天早晨”（民数记 11:9）时，你能付出什么努力呢？

paintings.title: we remember the fish
paintings.poem:
the cucumbers.
the melons.
the leeks, the onions, the garlic.

funny how
you can remember
every vegetable

and forget
the whip.

nothing at all
but this manna,
they said,

holding
bread from heaven
in their hands.

be careful
what you call
nothing.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Numbers 11:5-6, the story turns on the daily loaf broken in the hand—and ends with, “be careful what you call nothing.” What small, unhurried faithfulness is God inviting you into today?
paintings.zh_poem:
黄瓜。
瓜类。
韭菜，洋葱，大蒜。

有趣的是
你可以记得
每一种蔬菜

并忘记
鞭子。

什么都没有
但这吗哪，
他们说，

持有
从天上来的面包
在他们手中。

小心点
你叫什么
什么也没有。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在民数记 11 章 5-6 节中，故事以每天用手擘开的面包为中心，并以“要小心你所谓的无为”。神今天邀请你进入什么样的小而从容的信实呢？

paintings.title: not alone
paintings.poem:
it's too heavy,
Moses said.

I can't carry them
alone.

and God
didn't tell him
to try harder.

he said,
gather seventy.

and took
of the Spirit
that was on Moses
and put it on them.

sometimes
the answer to your prayer
is other people.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The world measures life by speed and noise, yet Numbers 11:17 points us to the quiet centerpiece of “not alone” and whispers, “sometimes the answer to your prayer is other people.” How can you practice that unhurried wisdom today?
paintings.zh_poem:
它太重了，
摩西说。

我无法携带它们
独自一人。

和上帝
没有告诉他
更加努力。

他说，
聚七十。

并采取了
圣灵的
那是在摩西身上
并把它放在他们身上。

有时
你祈祷的答案
是其他人。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 世界通过速度和噪音来衡量生命，然而民数记 11:17 却向我们指出了“不孤单”的安静核心，并轻声说道：“有时，你祈祷的答案是其他人。”今天你如何能修习这种从容的智慧呢？

paintings.title: very humble
paintings.poem:
his own sister and brother
spoke against him.

he didn't answer back.
God did.

and when Miriam
was shut outside the camp,
Moses was the one who cried,
heal her.

and the whole people
waited seven days
until she was
brought back in.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The poem closes with a quiet turn: “and the whole people waited seven days until she was brought back in.” Where in your life right now does that line hit closest to home?
paintings.zh_poem:
他自己的妹妹和弟弟
反对他。

他没有回答。
上帝做到了。

当米丽娅姆
被关在营外，
摩西是那个哭泣的人，
治愈她。

和全体人民
等了7天
直到她
带回来的。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 这首诗以一个安静的转折结束：“全体人民等待了七天，直到她被带回来。”现在，这条线在你生活中的哪个地方最贴近你的家？

paintings.title: Eshcol
paintings.poem:
one cluster of grapes
so big

it took
two men
and a pole.

and pomegranates.
and figs.

forty days in the land,
and this is what
they carried home.

proof.

every good thing
God had promised

was hanging
right there
between them.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Sometimes a single sentence opens a window in a closed room: how does “every good thing God had promised was hanging right there between them” (Numbers 13:23) speak to a question you have been carrying lately?
paintings.zh_poem:
一串葡萄
这么大

花了
两个男人
和一根杆子。

和石榴。
和无花果。

在这片土地上四十天，
这就是
他们带回家。

证明。

每一件好事
神曾应许

被挂着
就在那里
他们之间。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 有时候，一句话就能在封闭的房间里打开一扇窗：“神所应许的一切美善都挂在他们中间”（民数记 13:23）如何解答你最近一直提出的一个问题？

paintings.title: grasshoppers
paintings.poem:
twelve went.
twelve saw
the same fruit,
the same walls.

ten came back
and said,
we were like grasshoppers.

Caleb said,
let's go up at once.

same land.
same giants.

the difference
wasn't what they saw.

it was
who they thought
was going with them.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Hold your hands open for a moment before “grasshoppers” (Numbers 13:30-33): what are you gripping tightly that loosens when you hear, “it was who they thought was going with them”?
paintings.zh_poem:
十二去了。
十二锯
同样的水果，
相同的墙壁。

十回来了
并说，
我们就像蚱蜢一样。

迦勒说，
我们赶紧上去吧。

同一块土地。
同样的巨人。

区别
不是他们所看到的。

原来是
他们认为谁
和他们一起去。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在“蚱蜢”面前张开你的双手（民数记 13:30-33）：当你听到“是他们以为要和他们一起走的人”时，你紧握的是什么东西松开了？

paintings.title: the rod that budded
paintings.poem:
twelve dry sticks
left overnight
in the tent.

in the morning
one of them
was a tree.

buds,
blossoms,
and ripe almonds,

all at once,
on wood
cut and dry
and lying still.

God chooses
by making
something live.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Scripture remembers this moment in Numbers 17:8 not to impress us, but to steady us: when have you seen the truth that “God chooses by making something live” in your own story?
paintings.zh_poem:
十二根干棍
留下过夜
在帐篷里。

早上
其中之一
是一棵树。

芽,
开花，
和熟杏仁，

一下子，
在木头上
切割并干燥
并静静地躺着。

神选择
通过制作
活着的东西。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 圣经记得民数记 17:8 中的这一刻，不是为了给我们留下深刻的印象，而是为了让我们坚定：你什么时候在你自己的故事中看到过“神选择让某些东西活起来”的真理？

paintings.title: abundantly
paintings.poem:
the people were quarreling.
Moses was angry.

he was told
to speak to the rock,
and he struck it twice.

and still
the water came.
not a trickle.
abundantly.

Moses paid a price that day.
but God did not let
the people go thirsty.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As your pilgrim lantern pauses at “abundantly” (Numbers 20:11), what one honest sentence would you pray beside the quiet centerpiece of “abundantly” after reading, “but God did not let the people go thirsty”?
paintings.zh_poem:
人们在争吵。
摩西很生气。

他被告知
与岩石说话，
他敲了两下。

仍然
水来了。
不是细流。
丰富地。

那天摩西付出了代价。
但上帝没有让
人们口渴了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 当你的朝圣灯笼停在“丰盛”（民数记 20:11）处时，读完“但神没有让百姓渴了”之后，除了“丰盛”这个安静的核心词之外，你还会祈祷哪一句诚实的句子呢？

paintings.title: look and live
paintings.poem:
they were tired and angry,
and the desert
was full of snakes.

God did not
take the desert away.

he gave them
something to look at:
a bronze pole
lifted up where all could see.

no medicine.
no climbing.

turn your eyes,
and live.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Between the opening line (“they were tired and angry, and the desert was full of snakes”) and the closing thought (“no medicine. turn your eyes, and live”), what is Numbers 21:8-9 gently reframing in your own day?
paintings.zh_poem:
他们又累又生气，
和沙漠
到处都是蛇。

上帝没有
把沙漠拿走。

他给了他们
值得一看的东西：
一根青铜杆
被举到所有人都能看见的地方。

没有药。
没有攀爬。

转动你的眼睛，
并生活。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在开场白（“他们又累又生气，沙漠里到处是蛇”）和结束语（“没有药物。转动你的眼睛，就能活下去”）之间，民数记 21:8-9 在你那个时代轻轻地重构了什么？

paintings.title: spring up, well
paintings.poem:
this time
no one complained.

God said,
gather the people,
I will give them water.

and they sang
to a hole in the ground.

spring up.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Along the road of Fire by Night, “spring up, well” (Numbers 21:16-17) slows us down at the stone well in the heat of the day to remind us: “and they sang to a hole in the ground. spring up.” Where are you being invited to trade control for trust today?
paintings.zh_poem:
这次
没有人抱怨。

神说，
聚集人民，
我会给他们水。

他们唱
到地面上的一个洞。

涌现。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 沿着夜间火光之路，“泉涌吧，井”（民数记 21：16-17）让我们在炎热的白天在石井旁放慢脚步，提醒我们：“他们对着地上的一个洞唱歌。涌泉吧。”今天你被邀请在哪里用控制权换取信任？

paintings.title: the donkey
paintings.poem:
three times
she turned aside.

three times
he struck her.

he thought
she was being stubborn.

she was
saving his life.

the only one
on that road
who could see the angel

was the donkey.

be slow to hit
what's stopping you.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If you were walking this road with a close friend and stopped at “the donkey” (Numbers 22:28), what would you talk about after reading, “be slow to hit what's stopping you”?
paintings.zh_poem:
三次
她转过身去。

三次
他打了她。

他想
她很固执。

她是
救了他的命。

唯一的一个
在那条路上
谁能看见天使

是驴子。

击球要慢
是什么阻止了你。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果你和一位亲密的朋友一起走在这条路上，并在“驴子”处停下来（民数记 22:28），读完“慢慢地击打阻挡你的事物”后，你会谈论什么？

paintings.title: I can't reverse it
paintings.poem:
a king
paid a prophet
to curse them.

three times
he climbed a mountain.

three times
he opened his mouth,

and blessing
came out instead.

no one
can hire
a curse on you

strong enough
to undo
what God
has already said.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Pause before the long climb up the hill: what changes in your posture today when you sit with the closing words of “I can't reverse it”—“no one can hire a curse on you strong enough to undo what God has already said”?
paintings.zh_poem:
一个国王
付钱给先知
来诅咒他们。

三次
他爬上了一座山。

三次
他张开嘴，

和祝福
反而出来了。

没有人
可以雇用
对你的诅咒

足够强大
撤消
什么上帝
已经说过了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在漫长的爬山之前暂停一下：今天，当你坐下来并以“我无法扭转它”作为结束语时，你的姿势有什么变化——“没有人能对你施加足够强大的咒语来撤销上帝已经说过的话”？

paintings.title: but not near
paintings.poem:
from the top of a hill
a man who came to curse
saw a star.

not now.
not near.

far off,
rising
out of Jacob.

some promises
you only see
from a distance.

the star
was still coming.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look at the stillness of the quiet stars overhead in Timothy’s painting: what striving can you lay down as you ponder, “the star was still coming” (Numbers 24:17)?
paintings.zh_poem:
从山顶
一个来咒骂的人
看到一颗星星。

现在不要。
不近。

遥远的地方，
上升
从雅各那里出来。

一些承诺
你只看到
从远处。

星星
仍然来了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 看看提摩太画中头顶上安静的星星：当你沉思“星星仍来”（民数记 24:17）时，你还能付出什么努力呢？

paintings.title: the daughters speak right
paintings.poem:
Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah,
Milcah, Tirzah.

five sisters
with no brother
and no share of the land.

they stood at the door of the tent,
in front of everyone,
and asked.

Moses brought it to God.

and God said,
they're right,

and wrote it into the law
for every daughter after them.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Numbers 27:7, the story turns on the open threshold—and ends with, “and God said, they're right, and wrote it into the law for every daughter after them.” What small, unhurried faithfulness is God inviting you into today?
paintings.zh_poem:
玛拉、诺亚、霍格拉、
密迦、得撒。

五姐妹
没有兄弟
并且没有土地份额。

他们站在帐篷门口，
在所有人面前，
并问道。

摩西把它带到上帝面前。

神说，
他们是对的

并将其写入法律
为他们之后的每一个女儿。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在民数记 27 章 7 节中，故事从敞开的门槛开始，并以“上帝说，他们是对的，并将这写进了他们之后每一个女儿的律法”。神今天邀请你进入什么样的小而从容的信实呢？

paintings.title: a shepherd
paintings.poem:
told he would not
go into the land,

Moses didn't argue
for himself.

he prayed
for them.

give them someone
to go out before them
and bring them in.

don't leave them
like sheep
with no shepherd.

then he laid his hands
on Joshua

and let go.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The world measures life by speed and noise, yet Numbers 27:16-17 points us to your own two hands and whispers, “then he laid his hands on Joshua and let go.” How can you practice that unhurried wisdom today?
paintings.zh_poem:
告诉他不会
进入土地，

摩西没有争辩
为了他自己。

他祈祷
对于他们来说。

给他们一个人
在他们之前出去
并把他们带进来。

不要离开他们
像羊一样
没有牧羊人。

然后他把手放下
关于约书亚

然后放手。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 世界通过速度和噪音来衡量生命，然而民数记 27:16-17 却向我们指出了你自己的两只手，并低声说道：“然后他按手在约书亚身上，就放开了。”今天你如何能修习这种从容的智慧呢？

paintings.title: cities of refuge
paintings.poem:
even in the law
there was a door
left open.

six towns,
three on each side
of the Jordan,

for the one
who never meant it,
running,
with nowhere else to go.

get inside,
and you are safe.

the long road
ends with a place
to run to.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The poem closes with a quiet turn: “the long road ends with a place to run to.” Where in your life right now does that line hit closest to home?
paintings.zh_poem:
即使在法律上
有一扇门
保持打开状态。

六个城镇，
每边三个
约旦河的,

为了一个
谁从来没有这个意思，
跑步，
无处可去。

进去，
你很安全。

漫长的路
以一个地方结束
跑到。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 这首诗以一个安静的转折结束：“长路的尽头是一个可以奔向的地方。”现在，这条线在你生活中的哪个地方最贴近你的家？

zh_subtitle: 利未记与民数记诗画集
zh_beforeYouBegin:
利未记和民数记是关于西奈山营地和之后的漫长道路的书。他们在祭坛上点燃永不熄灭的火，一把用盐调味的面粉，一只独自走入沙漠的山羊，为穷人留下的田野角落，以及每五十年吹响自由的号角。然后营地出发：向人们发出祝福，白天有云，晚上有火，露水里有吗哪，杆子上扛着一串葡萄，一根长满杏花的干杆，水从岩石中倾泻而下，一头驴停在路上，六座城门敞开，供任何需要奔跑的人使用。

本书用四十首短诗，分为五部分来详细介绍它们：两首是《利未记》，三首是《民数记》。每首诗都位于一幅画旁边和一行经文之下。

这些诗不是圣经。它们是一位读者对此的回应。打开这本书旁边的利未记和民数记，让真正的话语成为最后的话语。
